explanations.3: This disables interactive prompts during package installation so the build doesn't pause waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && connects commands so they all run together, and the backslash lets us continue this command on the next line.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the package cache files to make the final image smaller.
explanations.14: We're running a script from the internet using curl; the empty quotes pass no custom arguments to the install script.
explanations.15: The --unattended flag installs Oh-My-Zsh without prompting, and --keep-zshrc preserves any existing shell configuration.
explanations.20: This sed command finds the plugins line in the config file and modifies it in-place (-i) to add our new plugin to the list.
explanations.25: The printf command with %s\n creates multiple lines of text; each argument becomes a line with a newline after it.
explanations.41: The > redirects all those printed lines into the config file instead of printing them to the screen.
explanations.45: We're appending (>>) this PROMPT line to the zshrc file, which tells the shell what the command prompt should look like.
explanations.47: The flags mean: -i for interactive mode (keep stdin open), -l for login shell (loads full environment), and /bin/zsh is the program to run.
